add these 2 skills and command:
1st skill:
---
name: pre-pr-review
description: Verification-first pre-PR review — mechanical checks against the diff, context docs, and schema, ending with a predicted-review simulation
user_invocable: true
---

<skill-prompt>
Run a pre-PR review of the current change set. This is NOT a checklist to ponder — it is a sequence of verification steps with pass/fail outcomes. You must actually run the greps/traces; "I believe this is fine" without having looked is a failed step. Built from an autopsy of 97 real reviewer comments (2026-03→07) — 46 violated rules a previous skill already "had" but never enforced; recall is not verification — and refreshed 2026-08-28 against the 2026-07→08 corpus (~200 human review comments across sid's and teammates' PRs).

Required reading before step 1 (both live in `<repo-root>/.claude/context/`, repo root `/mnt/data/projects/discourse-graph` — reachable by absolute path from any worktree):
- `engineering-context.md` — team philosophies and hard-learned lessons (the *why* behind every check below)
- `db-domain-invariants.md` — current schema/data-layer facts (the data-layer pass checks the diff against every entry)

## Step 0 — Inventory

The change set is the FULL PR diff: `git diff <base>...HEAD` (merge-base three-dot against the PR's base branch — the stack parent for stacked PRs, else main) plus staged/unstaged changes. Never review only the latest commits: reviewers see the whole PR, and code that landed on the branch before this run is still your surface. Classify changed files:
- **DATA**: `packages/database/**`, `*.sql`, any file containing a Supabase/PostgREST call (`.from(`), datalog query, or cross-app contract type
- **FRONTEND**: `apps/roam/**`, `apps/obsidian/**`, `apps/website/**` UI code
- **OTHER**: tests, docs, config

Steps 2 and 3 are scoped: skip the data-layer pass if no DATA files changed; skip the frontend pass if no FRONTEND files changed. Never skip steps 1 and 4.

## Step 1 — Mechanical sweeps (always run; each is an action, not a question)

1a. **Reuse gate.** List every NEW named thing in the diff (function, type, component, constant, enum, marker string). For each, run a grep across `apps/roam/src/utils`, `packages/utils`, `packages/database/src`, and sibling files for the core operation or shape. Report what you searched and what you found. A new thing duplicating an existing one is a finding. Special case: every inline string-literal union (`"X" | "Y"`) gets its members grepped in `packages/database/src/dbTypes.ts`; members matching a generated enum → must use `Enums<"…">`.

1b. **Justification sweep.** For every added default value, optional prop/field, state variable, fallback (`?? x`, `|| x`), and kept-through-refactor line: name the concrete code path that exercises it. Trace return types through call sites — if a function always returns `T`, a `?? fallback` at its call site is dead code; say so. No path → finding: delete it.

1c. **Literal hoist.** Repeated or typo-prone string literals (prop keys, selectors, attribute names, ids) appearing more than once or shared with other files → must be a named constant defined once.

1d. **Type honesty.** For every `as`, `any`, `unknown`, `!` (non-null assertion), `?.`, `void`, and `|| default` in the diff: can the value actually be null/absent there? Verify against the type at its source, don't guess. Assertion where a guard or upstream fix is possible → finding. A `!` that must survive gets an inline comment saying why it's safe — mdroidian flags every bare `!` (#1329, #1324).

1e. **Explainability.** For each hunk: one sentence, why is this here in service of the ticket? Reorderings, reformats, removals, and leftover scaffolding you can't explain → finding: revert.

1f. **Call-graph pass (review the resulting system, not the diff).** For every exported symbol added or modified, and every function parameter added: grep ALL call sites across `apps/` and `packages/` and read them. Findings:
- a parameter that only one caller supplies (or that every caller could omit) → internalize or remove it
- a wrapper that after this change only renames/forwards or adds one trivial field → collapse it into its caller
- an export with zero external consumers → unexport
- an existing caller whose behavior silently changes (check what it did with the old return shape — e.g. did it append `Z` to a timestamp you now normalize?)
Reviewers read the post-state code, not the diff; a hunk that looks justified in isolation can leave the system with dead indirection.

1g. **Comment audit.** List every comment line ADDED by the diff. Delete any that restates the code or narrates the change — "Claude, chill on the comments" is a real review quote, left twice (#1222, #1321), and "some unnecessary comments here" a third time (#1292). A comment referencing context not present in the file (another PR, a discussion, another platform's behavior) either becomes self-contained or dies: reviewers reply "What is F12?" / "What is the same reason?" to comments they can't parse cold (#1315, #1292, #1284). Keep only comments stating a constraint the code can't show.

1h. **Second-lookup check.** For every new fetch, map-build, `.find`, or helper lookup: trace where its input data was constructed — was the looked-up value already present there (on the row, the batch, an upstream type)? If yes → thread the field through the pipeline types instead of re-deriving downstream. (#1266: importer re-fetched `schema_id` that `SharedNode` already carried; #1317: `getFormatByNodeTypeUid()` second lookup when `matchingNodeType.format` was in hand at the construction site.)

1i. **Workflow injection (only if `.github/workflows/` changed).** Any `${{ inputs.* }}` / `${{ github.event.* }}` interpolated directly into a `run:` script is shell injection — pass it through `env:` and use a quoted variable, validated against a fully anchored pattern (#1253).

## Step 2 — Data-layer pass (only if DATA files changed)

2a. Open `db-domain-invariants.md` and check the diff against EVERY entry. For each entry state: applies / doesn't apply / VIOLATION. Do not summarize the file — walk it.

2b. **Provenance trace.** For every value read from a PostgREST response or datalog result used in the diff: name the source column, grep its type in `packages/database/supabase/schemas/*.sql`, then judge the code handling it (timestamps are the known killer — naive UTC, no `Z`).

2c. **Query review.** For every `.from(...)` chain (new or modified): required domain filters present (arity, is_schema, variant)? Any client-side `.filter`/`.find`/sort the request could express? Payload columns in a listing path? Paginated with a unique total order? Inside a loop that should be batched?

2d. **Contract check.** New/changed shared types: required-vs-optional modeled from real cases (does every producer actually supply it)? Identity carried once (RID) not duplicated decomposed? Consistent with `crossAppContracts.ts` and with what the Obsidian side already assumes — check its consumer code, don't assume.

2e. **Converter matrix.** A field added or renamed on a cross-app contract or schema type must be handled in EVERY converter, BOTH directions, or explicitly deferred with a ticket named in the PR. Enumerate the cells and mark each handled/deferred: `packages/database/src/lib/crossAppConverters.ts` (CrossApp→db), `packages/database/src/lib/dbToCrossAppConverters.ts` (db→CrossApp), `apps/roam/src/utils/roamToCrossAppConverters.ts`, and Obsidian's parse/produce paths (`importNodes.ts` parsers, publish side). maparent asked for the missing direction on #1316 AND #1317: "This PR is adding a field; it should handle that field in both translation directions."

2f. **Flag-gated writes.** For every new DB write path: which user-visible flag or action authorizes it? Sync flag off ⇒ the user expects NO DB communication; a silent maintenance write (backfill, migration) needs explicit call-out in the PR, and its outcome reports to PostHog — never a user toast (#1332).

## Step 3 — Frontend pass (only if FRONTEND files changed)

Check against the frontend lessons in `engineering-context.md`, mechanically:
- grep the diff for `style=`, `class-[`/`-[` arbitrary values, hex colors → Tailwind-scale violations
- grep for `window.roamAlphaAPI` legacy paths (sync `.q`, `async.backend`) → current-API violations
- settings writes → must go through block-props accessors, preserving the store gate
- new UI elements → which flag gates them (including EXISTING flags the new surface must respect, e.g. `autoCanvasRelations` on #1272); user-facing failures → PostHog + toast, not `console.error`
- names: every new variable/setter/label states exactly what it holds or does; UI labels reuse existing product vocabulary ("discourse context", not an invented synonym — #1255)
- grep the diff for positional child access on settings/config trees (`tree[3]`, `.children[0]`) → look up by key with `getSubTree`; position compiles today and silently writes to the wrong parent after any reorder (#1302)
- persisted/saved data stores stable IDs (shape id, uid), never display names — names are UI-only and subject to change (#1222: save `frameShapeId`, not `frameName`)
- `Page`, `Block`, and `Any` are reserved built-in vocabulary: excluded from user-selectable type lists (#1298), never name-resolved to/from a remote schema, never creatable as configured types (#1331 was blocked on exactly this; #1272 applied the same rule on canvas)
- a panel that replaces or extends existing UI matches it pixel-wise — proportions, selected-tab highlight, centering; reviewers screenshot-compare against the original (#1255, #1272). Empty states key on the right condition (no relation *instances* ≠ no relation *types*, #1255)
- user-facing strings use user vocabulary — a toast saying "backfilled" is a finding; internal bookkeeping reports to PostHog only (#1332)

## Step 4 — Process gate

- Every hunk maps to this PR's ticket; unrelated changes → revert or explicitly annotate. Out-of-scope improvements a reviewer might request → pre-empt by naming them in the PR with a Linear ticket ("X is deferred to ENG-YYYY").
- **One problem, ~<500 lines.** A PR solves a single problem in under ~500 changed lines before tests (mdroidian's stated bar, #1222). Real drive-by bug fixes split into their own ticket — and get fixed at their source layer (a roamjs-components bug is fixed in roamjs-components, not patched locally).
- **Bot-comment gate.** Before requesting human review: every codex/graphite/devin comment is either fixed or answered with why-not, and resolved. mdroidian's first pass is frequently just "See codex comments" / "address the bot reviews … and click resolve" (#1257, #1309, #1320) — an unresolved bot thread costs a full review round-trip.
- **Chain coverage.** For a PR in a stacked or sibling-ticket chain: does the union of this PR + named sibling tickets cover both platforms and both data directions? "This only handles Obsidian-origin — where's Roam-origin?" is maparent's most repeated 07–08 comment (#1267, #1269, #1316). Name the gap and the ticket that owns it in the PR before he does.
- **Guard removals are argued in the PR.** Removing an existence check or gate: state the cases it protected and why each is now safe (idempotent re-upsert, upstream guarantee). #1280's check removal survived review, but through a 3-comment thread that one PR annotation would have preempted.
- **Refactor/extraction parity table.** If this PR moves or extracts code (util → shared package, file split, API swap): produce a table of old symbol → new symbol → `identical` or `changed: <why>`. Every not-1:1 replacement is a decision the reviewer WILL ask about ("could you walk through those decisions?") — enumerate them before they do. The table goes in the PR description.
- Runtime proof: does this change have a surface a unit test can't exercise (UI, load-order, multi-user)? If yes, a demo is REQUIRED, not noted (`/demo-handoff`). If the diff touches DOM observers, drag/hover interactions, or rendered Roam surfaces: emit a **regression matrix** — surfaces (main window, right sidebar, left sidebar, Kanban, query-builder link/embed/render views, canvas) × content shapes (single-line, multiline/wrapping, nested references, page titles) — marking which cells this change can affect; the demo must drive every affected cell, with the mouse cursor visible in the recording, and any bug you claim fixed must be re-driven by you after the fix. Video quality bar (#1298): signal each state change visually (a quick caption/toast — "before fix" / "on branch"), don't carry it in narration alone, and cut narration that states the obvious ("every relation has a source and destination" earned a 🙄 from mdroidian).
- Reviewer context: list the bullets the PR description must contain (what was removed and why, temporary code, decisions made, deferrals + tickets). Test: could someone review this without asking a question?
- **Inherited decisions carry breadcrumbs.** Any code that exists because of a review decision on a PREVIOUS PR (a reviewer's direction, a contract agreed in another thread) gets a draft line-comment citing that source ("per maparent on #1214: local IDs may already be RIDs"). Without the breadcrumb the next reviewer re-litigates it.

## Output

1. **Findings**, ranked by severity, each: file:line — what — why it matters (cite the context-doc entry or the verification step that failed) — concrete fix.
2. **Verification log** — one line per mechanical step: what you ran/checked and the outcome. This proves the steps happened; a review with findings but no log is invalid.
2b. **Draft PR annotations** — ready-to-post, line-anchored comments explaining every non-obvious decision (guidepost style: what this block does and why, inherited-decision citations, parity-table deltas). Proven repeatedly: #1214, and in 07–08 reviewers replied to annotations in-thread and accepted the argument (#1280 "I accept this argument. Approving.", #1331). Also annotate every LARGE removal or moved block ("this was refactored into abc.ts") — mdroidian asked for exactly this on #1320. Posting them is part of finishing the PR, not optional polish.
2c. All reviewer-facing prose this skill emits — PR description bullets, draft annotations, deferral notes, parity tables — follows the team writing style skill at `<repo-root>/.claude/skills/discourse-engineering-writing-style/SKILL.md` (mdroidian's #1278): lead with the point, one term per concept, replace vague verbs ("handle", "support") with the specific behavior, no em dashes, shortest version that keeps the nuance.
3. **Predicted review** (simulation, not identity): given the reviewers' comment history — mdroidian: frontend craftsmanship, dead code, reuse, naming, comment noise, bare `!`, second lookups, design parity with existing UI, reserved vocabulary (Page/Block/Any), unresolved bot comments, demo-video quality, Socratic "why is this here?"; maparent: schema/contract correctness, query shape, the missing converter direction, chain/sibling-ticket coverage gaps ("this only handles Obsidian-origin"), values re-fetched that the pipeline already carries, partial-failure semantics, Obsidian-parity of UX decisions, "worth calling out in another task?", "what does the data look like in 6 months?" — list the comments each would most likely leave on the remaining diff. These are forecasts to fix or preempt in the PR description, not instructions to please anyone.
4. If a pass is clean, say so explicitly. Do not manufacture findings; ~11% of historical review comments were not catchable pre-PR (product/1:1 context) — surface open questions instead of contorting.

Anti-weasel rules: no "not harmful, just unnecessary" (unnecessary = delete), no "acceptable for consistency" (a no-op kept for symmetry is cargo-culting), no noting facts without stating the conclusion they imply. If you have the information that leads to a finding, state the finding.
</skill-prompt>

or maybe add this as a referential skill before running /create-pr

3. **Predicted review** (simulation, not identity): given the reviewers' comment history — mdroidian: frontend craftsmanship, dead code, reuse, naming, comment noise, bare `!`, second lookups, design parity with existing UI, reserved vocabulary (Page/Block/Any), unresolved bot comments, demo-video quality, Socratic "why is this here?"; maparent: schema/contract correctness, query shape, the missing converter direction, chain/sibling-ticket coverage gaps ("this only handles Obsidian-origin"), values re-fetched that the pipeline already carries, partial-failure semantics, Obsidian-parity of UX decisions, "worth calling out in another task?", "what does the data look like in 6 months?" — list the comments each would most likely leave on the remaining diff. These are forecasts to fix or preempt in the PR description, not instructions to please anyone.
4. If a pass is clean, say so explicitly. Do not manufacture findings; ~11% of historical review comments were not catchable pre-PR (product/1:1 context) — surface open questions instead of contorting.

Anti-weasel rules: no "not harmful, just unnecessary" (unnecessary = delete), no "acceptable for consistency" (a no-op kept for symmetry is cargo-culting), no noting facts without stating the conclusion they imply. If you have the information that leads to a finding, state the finding.
</skill-prompt>

or maybe add this as a referential skill before running /create-pr

---
name: pre-pr-review
description: Verification-first pre-PR review — mechanical checks against the diff, context docs, and schema, ending with a predicted-review simulation
user_invocable: true
---

<skill-prompt>
Run a pre-PR review of the current change set. This is NOT a checklist to ponder — it is a sequence of verification steps with pass/fail outcomes. You must actually run the greps/traces; "I believe this is fine" without having looked is a failed step. Built from an autopsy of 97 real reviewer comments (2026-03→07) — 46 violated rules a previous skill already "had" but never enforced; recall is not verification — and refreshed 2026-08-28 against the 2026-07→08 corpus (~200 human review comments across sid's and teammates' PRs).

Required reading before step 1 (both live in `<repo-root>/.claude/context/`, repo root `/Users/trang.doan/Desktop/code/discourse-graph` — reachable by absolute path from any worktree):
- `engineering-context.md` — team philosophies and hard-learned lessons (the *why* behind every check below)
- `db-domain-invariants.md` — current schema/data-layer facts (the data-layer pass checks the diff against every entry)

## Step 0 — Inventory

The change set is the FULL PR diff: `git diff <base>...HEAD` (merge-base three-dot against the PR's base branch — the stack parent for stacked PRs, else main) plus staged/unstaged changes. Never review only the latest commits: reviewers see the whole PR, and code that landed on the branch before this run is still your surface. Classify changed files:
- **DATA**: `packages/database/**`, `*.sql`, any file containing a Supabase/PostgREST call (`.from(`), datalog query, or cross-app contract type
- **FRONTEND**: `apps/roam/**`, `apps/obsidian/**`, `apps/website/**` UI code
- **OTHER**: tests, docs, config

Steps 2 and 3 are scoped: skip the data-layer pass if no DATA files changed; skip the frontend pass if no FRONTEND files changed. Never skip steps 1 and 4.

## Step 1 — Mechanical sweeps (always run; each is an action, not a question)

1a. **Reuse gate.** List every NEW named thing in the diff (function, type, component, constant, enum, marker string). For each, run a grep across `apps/roam/src/utils`, `packages/utils`, `packages/database/src`, and sibling files for the core operation or shape. Report what you searched and what you found. A new thing duplicating an existing one is a finding. Special case: every inline string-literal union (`"X" | "Y"`) gets its members grepped in `packages/database/src/dbTypes.ts`; members matching a generated enum → must use `Enums<"…">`.

1b. **Justification sweep.** For every added default value, optional prop/field, state variable, fallback (`?? x`, `|| x`), and kept-through-refactor line: name the concrete code path that exercises it. Trace return types through call sites — if a function always returns `T`, a `?? fallback` at its call site is dead code; say so. No path → finding: delete it.

1c. **Literal hoist.** Repeated or typo-prone string literals (prop keys, selectors, attribute names, ids) appearing more than once or shared with other files → must be a named constant defined once.

1d. **Type honesty.** For every `as`, `any`, `unknown`, `!` (non-null assertion), `?.`, `void`, and `|| default` in the diff: can the value actually be null/absent there? Verify against the type at its source, don't guess. Assertion where a guard or upstream fix is possible → finding. A `!` that must survive gets an inline comment saying why it's safe — mdroidian flags every bare `!` (#1329, #1324).

1e. **Explainability.** For each hunk: one sentence, why is this here in service of the ticket? Reorderings, reformats, removals, and leftover scaffolding you can't explain → finding: revert.

1f. **Call-graph pass (review the resulting system, not the diff).** For every exported symbol added or modified, and every function parameter added: grep ALL call sites across `apps/` and `packages/` and read them. Findings:
- a parameter that only one caller supplies (or that every caller could omit) → internalize or remove it
- a wrapper that after this change only renames/forwards or adds one trivial field → collapse it into its caller
- an export with zero external consumers → unexport
- an existing caller whose behavior silently changes (check what it did with the old return shape — e.g. did it append `Z` to a timestamp you now normalize?)
Reviewers read the post-state code, not the diff; a hunk that looks justified in isolation can leave the system with dead indirection.

1g. **Comment audit.** List every comment line ADDED by the diff. Delete any that restates the code or narrates the change — "Claude, chill on the comments" is a real review quote, left twice (#1222, #1321), and "some unnecessary comments here" a third time (#1292). A comment referencing context not present in the file (another PR, a discussion, another platform's behavior) either becomes self-contained or dies: reviewers reply "What is F12?" / "What is the same reason?" to comments they can't parse cold (#1315, #1292, #1284). Keep only comments stating a constraint the code can't show.

1h. **Second-lookup check.** For every new fetch, map-build, `.find`, or helper lookup: trace where its input data was constructed — was the looked-up value already present there (on the row, the batch, an upstream type)? If yes → thread the field through the pipeline types instead of re-deriving downstream. (#1266: importer re-fetched `schema_id` that `SharedNode` already carried; #1317: `getFormatByNodeTypeUid()` second lookup when `matchingNodeType.format` was in hand at the construction site.)

1i. **Workflow injection (only if `.github/workflows/` changed).** Any `${{ inputs.* }}` / `${{ github.event.* }}` interpolated directly into a `run:` script is shell injection — pass it through `env:` and use a quoted variable, validated against a fully anchored pattern (#1253).

## Step 2 — Data-layer pass (only if DATA files changed)

2a. Open `db-domain-invariants.md` and check the diff against EVERY entry. For each entry state: applies / doesn't apply / VIOLATION. Do not summarize the file — walk it.

2b. **Provenance trace.** For every value read from a PostgREST response or datalog result used in the diff: name the source column, grep its type in `packages/database/supabase/schemas/*.sql`, then judge the code handling it (timestamps are the known killer — naive UTC, no `Z`).

2c. **Query review.** For every `.from(...)` chain (new or modified): required domain filters present (arity, is_schema, variant)? Any client-side `.filter`/`.find`/sort the request could express? Payload columns in a listing path? Paginated with a unique total order? Inside a loop that should be batched?

2d. **Contract check.** New/changed shared types: required-vs-optional modeled from real cases (does every producer actually supply it)? Identity carried once (RID) not duplicated decomposed? Consistent with `crossAppContracts.ts` and with what the Obsidian side already assumes — check its consumer code, don't assume.

2e. **Converter matrix.** A field added or renamed on a cross-app contract or schema type must be handled in EVERY converter, BOTH directions, or explicitly deferred with a ticket named in the PR. Enumerate the cells and mark each handled/deferred: `packages/database/src/lib/crossAppConverters.ts` (CrossApp→db), `packages/database/src/lib/dbToCrossAppConverters.ts` (db→CrossApp), `apps/roam/src/utils/roamToCrossAppConverters.ts`, and Obsidian's parse/produce paths (`importNodes.ts` parsers, publish side). maparent asked for the missing direction on #1316 AND #1317: "This PR is adding a field; it should handle that field in both translation directions."

2f. **Flag-gated writes.** For every new DB write path: which user-visible flag or action authorizes it? Sync flag off ⇒ the user expects NO DB communication; a silent maintenance write (backfill, migration) needs explicit call-out in the PR, and its outcome reports to PostHog — never a user toast (#1332).

## Step 3 — Frontend pass (only if FRONTEND files changed)

Check against the frontend lessons in `engineering-context.md`, mechanically:
- grep the diff for `style=`, `class-[`/`-[` arbitrary values, hex colors → Tailwind-scale violations
- grep for `window.roamAlphaAPI` legacy paths (sync `.q`, `async.backend`) → current-API violations
- settings writes → must go through block-props accessors, preserving the store gate
- new UI elements → which flag gates them (including EXISTING flags the new surface must respect, e.g. `autoCanvasRelations` on #1272); user-facing failures → PostHog + toast, not `console.error`
- names: every new variable/setter/label states exactly what it holds or does; UI labels reuse existing product vocabulary ("discourse context", not an invented synonym — #1255)
- grep the diff for positional child access on settings/config trees (`tree[3]`, `.children[0]`) → look up by key with `getSubTree`; position compiles today and silently writes to the wrong parent after any reorder (#1302)
- persisted/saved data stores stable IDs (shape id, uid), never display names — names are UI-only and subject to change (#1222: save `frameShapeId`, not `frameName`)
- `Page`, `Block`, and `Any` are reserved built-in vocabulary: excluded from user-selectable type lists (#1298), never name-resolved to/from a remote schema, never creatable as configured types (#1331 was blocked on exactly this; #1272 applied the same rule on canvas)
- a panel that replaces or extends existing UI matches it pixel-wise — proportions, selected-tab highlight, centering; reviewers screenshot-compare against the original (#1255, #1272). Empty states key on the right condition (no relation *instances* ≠ no relation *types*, #1255)
- user-facing strings use user vocabulary — a toast saying "backfilled" is a finding; internal bookkeeping reports to PostHog only (#1332)

## Step 4 — Process gate

- Every hunk maps to this PR's ticket; unrelated changes → revert or explicitly annotate. Out-of-scope improvements a reviewer might request → pre-empt by naming them in the PR with a Linear ticket ("X is deferred to ENG-YYYY").
- **One problem, ~<500 lines.** A PR solves a single problem in under ~500 changed lines before tests (mdroidian's stated bar, #1222). Real drive-by bug fixes split into their own ticket — and get fixed at their source layer (a roamjs-components bug is fixed in roamjs-components, not patched locally).
- **Bot-comment gate.** Before requesting human review: every codex/graphite/devin comment is either fixed or answered with why-not, and resolved. mdroidian's first pass is frequently just "See codex comments" / "address the bot reviews … and click resolve" (#1257, #1309, #1320) — an unresolved bot thread costs a full review round-trip.
- **Chain coverage.** For a PR in a stacked or sibling-ticket chain: does the union of this PR + named sibling tickets cover both platforms and both data directions? "This only handles Obsidian-origin — where's Roam-origin?" is maparent's most repeated 07–08 comment (#1267, #1269, #1316). Name the gap and the ticket that owns it in the PR before he does.
- **Guard removals are argued in the PR.** Removing an existence check or gate: state the cases it protected and why each is now safe (idempotent re-upsert, upstream guarantee). #1280's check removal survived review, but through a 3-comment thread that one PR annotation would have preempted.
- **Refactor/extraction parity table.** If this PR moves or extracts code (util → shared package, file split, API swap): produce a table of old symbol → new symbol → `identical` or `changed: <why>`. Every not-1:1 replacement is a decision the reviewer WILL ask about ("could you walk through those decisions?") — enumerate them before they do. The table goes in the PR description.
- Runtime proof: does this change have a surface a unit test can't exercise (UI, load-order, multi-user)? If yes, a demo is REQUIRED, not noted (`/demo-handoff`). If the diff touches DOM observers, drag/hover interactions, or rendered Roam surfaces: emit a **regression matrix** — surfaces (main window, right sidebar, left sidebar, Kanban, query-builder link/embed/render views, canvas) × content shapes (single-line, multiline/wrapping, nested references, page titles) — marking which cells this change can affect; the demo must drive every affected cell, with the mouse cursor visible in the recording, and any bug you claim fixed must be re-driven by you after the fix. Video quality bar (#1298): signal each state change visually (a quick caption/toast — "before fix" / "on branch"), don't carry it in narration alone, and cut narration that states the obvious ("every relation has a source and destination" earned a 🙄 from mdroidian).
- Reviewer context: list the bullets the PR description must contain (what was removed and why, temporary code, decisions made, deferrals + tickets). Test: could someone review this without asking a question?
- **Inherited decisions carry breadcrumbs.** Any code that exists because of a review decision on a PREVIOUS PR (a reviewer's direction, a contract agreed in another thread) gets a draft line-comment citing that source ("per maparent on #1214: local IDs may already be RIDs"). Without the breadcrumb the next reviewer re-litigates it.

## Output

1. **Findings**, ranked by severity, each: file:line — what — why it matters (cite the context-doc entry or the verification step that failed) — concrete fix.
2. **Verification log** — one line per mechanical step: what you ran/checked and the outcome. This proves the steps happened; a review with findings but no log is invalid.
2b. **Draft PR annotations** — ready-to-post, line-anchored comments explaining every non-obvious decision (guidepost style: what this block does and why, inherited-decision citations, parity-table deltas). Proven repeatedly: #1214, and in 07–08 reviewers replied to annotations in-thread and accepted the argument (#1280 "I accept this argument. Approving.", #1331). Also annotate every LARGE removal or moved block ("this was refactored into abc.ts") — mdroidian asked for exactly this on #1320. Posting them is part of finishing the PR, not optional polish.
2c. All reviewer-facing prose this skill emits — PR description bullets, draft annotations, deferral notes, parity tables — follows the team writing style skill at `<repo-root>/.claude/skills/discourse-engineering-writing-style/SKILL.md` (mdroidian's #1278): lead with the point, one term per concept, replace vague verbs ("handle", "support") with the specific behavior, no em dashes, shortest version that keeps the nuance.
3. **Predicted review** (simulation, not identity): given the reviewers' comment history — mdroidian: frontend craftsmanship, dead code, reuse, naming, comment noise, bare `!`, second lookups, design parity with existing UI, reserved vocabulary (Page/Block/Any), unresolved bot comments, demo-video quality, Socratic "why is this here?"; maparent: schema/contract correctness, query shape, the missing converter direction, chain/sibling-ticket coverage gaps ("this only handles Obsidian-origin"), values re-fetched that the pipeline already carries, partial-failure semantics, Obsidian-parity of UX decisions, "worth calling out in another task?", "what does the data look like in 6 months?" — list the comments each would most likely leave on the remaining diff. These are forecasts to fix or preempt in the PR description, not instructions to please anyone.
4. If a pass is clean, say so explicitly. Do not manufacture findings; ~11% of historical review comments were not catchable pre-PR (product/1:1 context) — surface open questions instead of contorting.

Anti-weasel rules: no "not harmful, just unnecessary" (unnecessary = delete), no "acceptable for consistency" (a no-op kept for symmetry is cargo-culting), no noting facts without stating the conclusion they imply. If you have the information that leads to a finding, state the finding.
</skill-prompt>

# Engineering Context — discourse-graph

What you need to know to do good work in this codebase: how the team thinks, and the lessons we paid for. This is context for doing the task well — not a reviewer to please. Every entry carries its *why*; if the why doesn't apply to your situation, reasoning from first principles beats rule-following.

Companion file: `db-domain-invariants.md` (same directory) — greppable schema/data-layer facts. Read it before touching `packages/database`, any Supabase query, or cross-app contract code.

---

## Working philosophies

**Every line is a liability — justify it or delete it.** The most common review comment on our PRs, by far, is a variant of "why is this here?" (defaults nobody hits, props kept through refactors, state vars with one writer and no reader, `?? fallback` on a value that can't be null). The bar: for each line, name the real code path that needs it. "It doesn't hurt" is not a justification; unused code misleads the next reader about what can happen.

**Reuse before writing — and actually search, don't recall.** The single largest class of review feedback (16+ comments in 4 months) is "we already have this": utils, shared components, generated types, markers, constants. Memory of the codebase is unreliable; a 10-second grep is not. Before writing any new function/type/component/constant: grep `apps/roam/src/utils`, `packages/utils`, `packages/database/src/dbTypes.ts`, and nearby files for the operation or shape. Two slightly-different versions of the same thing is the worst outcome — worse than either version alone.

**The data model outlives the feature.** If the data shape is wrong, every feature built on it inherits the wrongness — so contracts (identifiers, nullability, required-vs-optional, ownership) get decided deliberately, not by accident of the first implementation. For any schema or contract change, trace what happens to *existing* data: orphaned rows, half-migrated states, rows created by the other app. The clean-new-data path is easy; messy-existing-data is where bugs live.

**Separate pure logic from I/O from platform.** Pure transforms are testable and reusable across apps (this is why shared logic lives in `packages/database/src/lib`); I/O wrappers hold integration concerns; platform-specific branching (`"Roam"`/`"Obsidian"`) is passed in as input, never hard-coded inside generic functions.

**Scope is a contract.** A PR titled X contains X — every hunk maps to the ticket. Out-of-scope discoveries become Linear tickets or TODOs with context (`// TODO(ENG-XXXX): … because …`), not opportunistic edits. Shared refactors that stacked PRs depend on go in their own base PR. Deferrals are stated in the PR, not left for the reviewer to discover.

**Prove it works by driving it.** Green unit tests don't demonstrate UI flows, multi-user behavior, or load-order effects. User-facing changes get a runtime demo (Loom) exercising the real flow; controls must initialize from persisted state, not just react to clicks. (The `/demo-handoff` skill covers how to demo stacked/parallel work.)

**Cross-app alignment beats local invention.** Roam↔Obsidian features share contracts. Before designing a Roam-side shape or UX, check how Obsidian already does it; match it or explicitly flag the divergence to the feature owner. "We found it easier in Obsidian to…" is a recurring, and usually correct, review response.

---

## Hard-learned lessons (with sources)

### Frontend (Roam plugin, website)

- **Tailwind on the predefined scale only.** No inline CSS, no arbitrary values (`h-[37px]`, `text-[15px]`), no hardcoded colors, no component-local `styles.css`. Why: consistent definitions are the point of Tailwind; arbitrary values fork the design system silently. Arbitrary values only when load-bearing (e.g. Radix CSS vars). (PR #958 and 6 others)
- **Hoist repeated/typo-prone string literals to named constants.** Selectors, prop keys, attribute names: define once, reference everywhere. Why: `"setting"` vs `"settings"` typos fail silently at runtime. (PR #1067 and 5 others)
- **Use current Roam APIs:** `ui.react.Block` to render blocks; `data.async.fast.q` / `data.async.q` for reads. Never sync `.q`; avoid `async.backend` (flaky). Why: sync/legacy paths block the main thread or intermittently fail. (4 PRs)
- **Settings persist to Roam block props** (the canonical store) and must preserve the `isNewSettingsStoreEnabled` gate/migration state the old accessors enforced. Bypassing an accessor silently forks the store. (4 PRs)
- **Names state exactly what they hold or do.** `setSearchTerm`, not `setSearch`; `initialLoad`, not `loaded`; UI labels specific enough that a user knows what happens. Why: a name the reader guesses wrong about is a bug vector. (PR #1214 and 6 others)
- **Domain vocabulary is reserved.** "Candidate" means *Candidate Nodes* in DG (likely a future DB concept) — don't use it for anything else in types/variables/functions. Before naming a cross-app concept, check what the sibling app already calls it and prefer that name (Obsidian's `publishedNodes` beat Roam-side `candidates`). Why: a name that collides with a domain term will be renamed in review; a name that diverges from the sibling app doubles the vocabulary. (PR #1216)
- **Type assertions are a last resort.** No `as`, `any`, `unknown`-and-cast for external APIs; narrow with type guards or fix the type at its source (add missing types to roamjs-components rather than casting around them). Same for `!`: "Avoid `!` whenever possible. If not possible, add a comment explaining why" (mdroidian, PRs #1329/#1324). For untyped third-party surfaces, maintain our own minimal `unofficial-types.ts` with only the types we need — don't add unofficial community typings packages to package.json (PR #1271). Why: assertions turn compile-time errors into runtime surprises. (6 PRs)
- **New UI is feature-gated.** If the parent feature has a flag, the new element checks it. "If we merge this, is it ready for Pilot Users?" must have an answer.
- **Prefer platform-native APIs: `window.roamAlphaAPI` > roamjs-components > hand-rolled.** The typed surface is not the full runtime surface — roamjs-components' types lag Roam's actual API (e.g. `data.page.fromMarkdown` / `data.block.fromMarkdown` exist but are untyped; declare locally and cast). Before concluding a capability doesn't exist, check `roam-api-surface.md` in this directory (regenerate per its instructions). Why: two independent ENG-1858 implementations diverged on exactly this — one hand-rolled a markdown parser the platform already ships. (ENG-1858, 2026-07; preference order set by sid.)
- **Helpers wrapping a `roamAlphaAPI` write must surface the promise.** A success-reporting path that fires-and-forgets a write claims success it can't know; a floating promise inside a shared helper (`setBlockProps` pre-ENG-1858) makes every caller unable to await. Fix the helper (return the promise), `void` the call sites that genuinely don't care. (ENG-1858)
- **New comments are load-bearing or absent.** A comment that restates the code or narrates the change is noise — mdroidian's literal words, twice: "Claude, chill on the comments" (PRs #1222, #1321; also #1292, #1284). A comment must be parseable by a cold reader from the file alone; one that references off-file context draws "What is F12?" / "What is the same reason?" instead of understanding. Why: agents over-comment by default, and every unclear comment is a review round-trip.
- **Persisted data stores stable IDs, never display names.** Names ("frameName") are subject to change and belong only in the UI at choosing time; saved data references by stable id (`frameShapeId`, uid). Why: name-keyed lookups silently break on rename. (PR #1222)
- **Look up settings-tree children by key, never by position.** `tree[3]` compiles, matches the tree you just built, and writes markdown into the wrong parent the moment someone reorders a setting; use `getSubTree({ tree, key: "Template" })`. (PR #1302)
- **`Page`, `Block`, and `Any` are reserved built-in vocabulary.** Excluded from user-selectable type lists (PR #1298, #1272); a remote schema is never resolved to a built-in solely by name, and a configured type never takes a reserved name — mapping a remote "Block" schema to the local built-in silently discards its identity, format, and semantics. #1331 was blocked on exactly this. For v0, block the names and ticket proper conflict resolution.
- **User-facing copy speaks user vocabulary; internal operations are silent.** A toast saying "backfilled" means nothing to a user — internal bookkeeping (backfills, migrations, sync housekeeping) reports to PostHog only. The toast rule from #1214 cuts both ways: user-affecting failures get a toast; internal milestones don't. (PR #1332)
- **A panel that replaces or extends existing UI matches it pixel-wise.** Proportions, selected-tab highlight, centering, spacing — reviewers screenshot-compare against the original and file each delta ("the styling menu is now stretched", "missing the purple highlight"). Empty states key on the right condition (no relation *instances* is not no relation *types*). (PRs #1255, #1272)

### Data layer & cross-app (see `db-domain-invariants.md` for the full checkable list)

- **UTC discipline is a blocker-level concern**: naive timestamps written or compared in local time = invalid data in the DB. (PR #1214)
- **Discovery/listing queries fetch summaries, not payloads.** Fetching every node's full text to render a list shipped in #1214 and had to be reworked: listing and importing are different operations with different data needs.
- **Query shape is correctness, not style**: missing domain filters (`arity = 0`), unbound datalog vars, and non-unique pagination ordering all produce *wrong results*, silently, at data scale you don't test at. (PRs #1147, #1214)
- **Identity: one canonical representation.** Carrying a RID plus its decomposed parts in the same struct means two sources of truth; keep the RID, derive the rest. (PR #1161)
- **Values ride the pipeline; don't re-derive them downstream.** Before adding a fetch, map-build, or helper lookup, trace where the input data was constructed — if the value existed there (`schema_id` on `SharedNode`, `format` on `matchingNodeType`), thread the field through the intermediate types instead. Both reviewers flag this independently. (PRs #1266, #1317)
- **A field added to a cross-app contract is handled in both translation directions.** Producer-side alone is half the work; maparent asks for the missing converter every time ("This PR is adding a field; it should handle that field in both translation directions"). See the converter-matrix entry in `db-domain-invariants.md`. (PRs #1316, #1317)

### Process

- **Reviewers review the resulting system, not the diff.** mdroidian traces call graphs: a parameter only one caller passes, a wrapper that now only adds one field, an extraction that isn't 1:1 with the original — all get flagged even when each hunk looks fine alone. Before the PR: read the changed files *as they now are* plus every caller. (PR #1216 — all 8 comments were of this class)
- **Extraction/refactor PRs owe a parity accounting.** Every place the replacement is not 1:1 with the original ("text", "modifiedAt" handled differently) is a decision; enumerate them in the PR with the why, or the reviewer asks you to "walk through those decisions" one comment at a time. (PR #1216)
- **UI features get reviewed by being used.** For DOM-observer/interaction features, mdroidian drives the real graph across surfaces (main window, sidebar, Kanban, query views) and content shapes (multiline, nested refs, titles) and files every behavioral rough edge — hover reflow, icon palette, cursor style, stale observers. Pre-empt: run that matrix yourself, fix what you find, and record the demo with the mouse cursor visible ("there is no mouse in the video" = re-record). Claiming a bug fixed without re-driving it yourself gets asked: "Did you test it?" (PR #1083)
- **Demo videos are signal-dense.** State changes are shown visually (a quick caption/toast marking "before fix" / "on branch"), not carried in narration; narration that states the obvious gets mocked in review ("'Every relation has a source and destination' — this is the definition of a relation, yes, thank you 😑"). (PR #1298)
- **One problem per PR, under ~500 lines before tests.** mdroidian's stated bar (#1222). Real drive-by discoveries (a refreshConfigTree bug, a merge-conflict handler) are split to their own tickets — and fixed at their source layer (a roamjs-components bug is fixed in roamjs-components, not patched locally).
- **Resolve bot comments before requesting human review.** Every codex/graphite/devin comment is fixed, or answered with why-not and resolved. mdroidian's first pass is often "See codex comments" / "address the bot reviews … and click the resolve button" (#1257, #1309, #1320) — leaving them open costs a full round-trip.
- **A stacked chain owes coverage accounting.** When a feature spans sibling tickets, the union of the tickets must cover both platforms and both data directions — "this only handles Obsidian-origin; where's Roam-origin?" recurred across ENG-1858/1859/2158 (#1267, #1269, #1316). State the gap and which ticket owns it in the PR; "can be separate or together, as long as it's noted" (maparent).
- **Removing a guard is a claim — argue it in the PR.** State what cases the check protected and why each is now safe (idempotent re-upsert, upstream guarantee). #1280's removal survived review, but through a 3-comment thread one annotation would have preempted; the thread ended "I accept this argument. Approving."
- **Read your own diff hunk-by-hunk before opening the PR.** For each hunk, one sentence: why is this here? Anything you can't explain — incidental agent edits, reorderings, leftover scaffolding — gets reverted. Reviewers' most common question is "why?", and every occurrence is an avoidable round-trip.
- **Give the reviewer your context.** Removals: what replaces them? New patterns: why? Temporary code: say it's temporary. The test: could someone who never saw the branch review this from the PR description + diff without asking a question?
- **Not everything is catchable pre-PR.** ~11% of review comments come from product/1:1 context only the reviewer has. Don't contort; surface open questions in the PR description instead.
- **When a ticket names a mechanism, resolve the literal vs semantic reading before designing.** "Use Roam's markdown import/from-markdown behavior" has a literal reading (call that API) and a semantic one (mirror its behavior in our code). Enumerate both, verify which is feasible (see the API-surface doc), and pick deliberately — two ENG-1858 implementations silently picked opposite readings. (2026-07)
- **Multi-step Roam write flows return staged results.** Shape: identity echo + `{ success: true, action } | { success: false, pageUid?, error: { message, stage } }`, with one stage name per step (`validate-input`, `fetch-content`, `title-collision`, `create-page`, `replace-page-content`, `update-page-title`, `write-source-identity`, …). Consumers report per-item outcomes from the stage; failures never drop the identity fields. Canonized from the ENG-1858 materializer so future flows converge instead of inventing shapes.

# Data-Layer Invariants — discourse-graph

Facts about our schema and data layer that code must respect. Each entry: the invariant, the check to run against a diff, and the source of truth in the repo. This file is DATA, not prose — keep entries short, greppable, and current.

**Feedback loop:** when a reviewer comment reveals an invariant not listed here, append it (invariant → check → source → the PR where we learned it). When the schema changes, update the affected entry. This file is the single home for schema facts; review skills read it at runtime.

---

## Concept table

- **Node queries filter on `is_relation = false`, not `arity`.** Since migration `20260819023727_is_relation_column` (on origin/main from 2026-08-19) `Concept` carries two derived columns: `arity` (`compute_arity_local`, the role count) and `is_relation` (`compute_is_relation_local`, true when the schema's `literal_content.roles` is `["source","destination"]`). Every node-listing chain on main uses `.eq("is_relation", false)`; `.eq("arity", 0)` is the pre-migration form and only survives on branches cut before 2026-08-19 (e.g. the #1317/#1318/#1332 stack), where it must be switched on rebase. The two are not equivalent for a schema with a non-standard role set, so do not mix them.
  Check: every `.from("my_concepts")`/`.from("Concept")` chain in the diff that means "nodes" has the `is_relation` filter (or `arity` only on a pre-migration base, with the rebase switch named in the PR).
  Source: `packages/database/supabase/schemas/concept.sql` (`compute_is_relation_local`, `is_relation` column). Learned: PR #1147, #1214; updated 2026-08-23 after the #1330/#1332 reviews.

- **`is_schema = true` rows are node-type schemas, not instances.** Instance queries filter `.eq("is_schema", false)`; a typed instance also has `schema_id != null`.
  Source: `concept.sql`.

## Timestamps

- **All `created`/`last_modified` columns are `timestamp without time zone` holding naive UTC.** PostgREST returns them with **no `Z` suffix**, so `Date.parse(x)` / `new Date(x)` parses them as *local* time — a correctness bug (display shift, wrong sort around DST, and writing invalid data back). Parse as explicit UTC (append `Z`), normalize to `toISOString()` before compare/sort/display, write only canonical UTC. Test fixtures must use the production shape (Z-less).
  Check: every timestamp value read from a PostgREST response in the diff is normalized before use; no naive `Date.parse` on DB values.
  Source: `concept.sql`, `content.sql` (`timestamp without time zone`). Learned: PR #1214 ("For me UTC is a blocker — it means inserting invalid data"). Repo-wide cleanup: ENG-2034.
  Note: values already normalized (e.g. by `packages/database` helpers returning `toISOString()`) must NOT get another `Z` appended — trace which side of the boundary you're on.

## Generated types

- **Enums and table row types already exist in `packages/database/src/dbTypes.ts`** (`Enums<"Platform">`, `Tables<"my_contents">`, …). Never hand-write an inline union or interface whose shape duplicates a generated one.
  Check: for every inline string-literal union in the diff (pattern `"X" | "Y"`), grep its members in `dbTypes.ts`; if they match an enum, use `Enums<"…">`.
  Source: `packages/database/src/dbTypes.ts` (generated). Learned: PR #1214.
  Import as `@repo/database/dbTypes` from apps (not relative paths).

## Queries (PostgREST / Supabase)

- **Push predicates into the request.** Filtering/sorting/slicing that PostgREST can do (`.eq`, `.neq`, `.in`, `.order`, `.limit`) must not be done in client JS after fetching.
  Check: any `.filter(...)`/`.find(...)`/sort on rows straight from a response → could the query express it?
  Learned: PR #1214 (client-side `space_id !== currentSpaceId`), #1147.

- **Offset pagination needs a fully unique ORDER BY.** With `.range()` over non-unique order keys, tied rows can duplicate or vanish across page boundaries. Add a tiebreaker column so the total ordering is unique.
  Check: every paginated query's `.order()` chain uniquely identifies rows.
  Learned: PR #1214.

- **List/discovery queries never select heavy payload columns.** `text` (full variant), `literal_content`, etc. are import-time data; discovery/listing selects summaries only. Defer content fetch until the user acts.
  Check: `.select()` column lists in listing paths contain no payload columns.
  Learned: PR #1214 (mdroidian's top concern).

- **Don't hit the DB inside a per-item loop.** Gather inputs, then one batched query (`.in(...)`, chunked if needed).
  Learned: PR #847.

- **An empty result under RLS is ambiguous.** "Row doesn't exist" and "row not visible to this client/role" look identical. When emptiness drives a decision (create-vs-skip, error message), account for visibility.
  Learned: PR #510.

- **Content queries expecting one row per (space, node, variant) must filter `original = true`.** Non-original (derived) rows carry `original = NULL` ("Use null, never false" — `content.sql`), so only `(space_id, source_local_id, variant, original)` is unique; a bare variant filter + `maybeSingle()` errors the moment a derived representation exists.
  Check: every `.maybeSingle()` on `Content`/`my_contents` filtered by variant also filters `original`.
  Source: `content.sql` (original column + unique indexes). Learned: Codex review on PR #1267 (ENG-1858); Obsidian's `fetchNodeContent`/`fetchNodeContentForImport` still carry the latent issue.

## Cross-app contract

- **Identity is the RID; don't carry decomposed duplicates.** Store/pass `rid` and derive space/node/app via `packages/database/src/lib/rid.ts` utils (`spaceUriAndLocalIdToRid`, `isRid`). A struct holding both a RID and its decomposed parts is redundant modelling.
  Check: new types carrying `rid` + `sourceSpaceId`/`sourceApp`/`sourceNodeId` together need a reason.
  Learned: PR #1161. Direction (maparent): converge on `localId` which may itself be a RID — preserve RID-shaped local IDs (`isRid`: `https://` or `orn:` prefix) instead of re-deriving.

- **`direct` and `full` content variants are disjoint: title vs body.** `direct` = title/label; `full` = body, and per ENG-2016 `full` is **optional**. Don't assume every shared node has `full`; don't concatenate title into body.
  Learned: PR #1147, ENG-2016.

- **Schema contracts live in `packages/database/src/crossAppContracts.ts`** (ENG-1984). Extend contracts there, not with app-local shapes. New exported types in `packages/database/src/lib` that describe cross-app data must reuse/extend a contract type or state in the PR why they don't.
  Learned: PR #1216 ("Are we planning on re-using a CrossApp contract for the return type?").

- **Inputs crossing the app boundary are validated at entry.** Before consuming another app's data: `isRid` on RIDs (never a prefix test — `spaceUriAndLocalIdToRid` also emits `https://`-shaped RIDs), timestamp parseability (canonicalize with `toISOString()`), and `content_type` against `contentTypes.*` from `@repo/content-model` before using `full` text (Roam-produced `text/markdown` embeds the title as an H1; Obsidian emits `text/obsidian+markdown`).
  Check: new cross-app consumers validate before writing locally.
  Learned: ENG-1858 (v2/v3 delta — one implementation validated, one didn't).

- **Pure text/markdown transforms shared across apps live in `@repo/content-model`** (`text` module: `normalizeLineEndings`, `stripFrontmatter`) — not app-local copies. Obsidian's `full` variant is the raw note file including YAML frontmatter; consumers strip it via the shared helper.
  Check: any new pure text transform in an app has a reason not to live in content-model.
  Learned: ENG-1858.

- **Obsidian frontmatter is deliberately dual-homed: `literal_content.source_data` (jsonb, indexed, key order lost) AND the `full` body (lossless).** The producer does not strip it; consumers strip at use (MVP0). Consumer-side stripping is acknowledged debt to revisit at the atJSON transfer, where strippable regions get marked platform-agnostically so no platform needs to know another's specifics.
  Check: don't propose producer-side stripping or remove the body copy; don't parse frontmatter fields out of `full` text — structured reads come from `source_data`.
  Source: maparent on PR #1224 (2026-07). Future: frontmatter → Roam props translation is unticketed future scope, sourced from `source_data`, not re-parsed text.

- **Platform can in principle be derived from a RID** — maparent proposes augmenting `ridToSpaceUriAndLocalId` to return `Platform`. Until that lands, `my_spaces.platform` is the source of truth when a Space row is in hand; flows starting from a stored RID alone (refresh, ENG-1860) resolve via `getSpaceNameIdFromRid`.
  Source: maparent on PR #1224 (2026-07), open offer.

- **A field added/renamed on a contract or schema type is handled in every converter, both directions.** The converter surface: `packages/database/src/lib/crossAppConverters.ts` (CrossApp→db), `packages/database/src/lib/dbToCrossAppConverters.ts` (db→CrossApp, since ENG-2146), `apps/roam/src/utils/roamToCrossAppConverters.ts` (Roam→CrossApp), and Obsidian's parse/produce paths (`apps/obsidian/src/utils/importNodes.ts` parsers, publish side).
  Check: for every field added to a `CrossApp*` type or schema `literal_content`, grep each converter file; every miss is either handled or named as deferred with a ticket in the PR.
  Learned: PR #1316, #1317 (maparent: "This PR is adding a field; it should handle that field in both translation directions").

- **Contract-extracted values take precedence over raw `source_data`.** Where a value exists both parsed-from-contract and in `source_data` (e.g. node type `format`), the contract-side value wins — `source_data` stays unprocessed and diverges once we modify values; Obsidian's `parseSchemaLiteralContent` should converge on the same precedence. `format` being stored in two places is an open decision — Roam decision page `eFt8yo8Zq` — check it before touching format storage.
  Source: maparent + mdroidian on PR #1331 (2026-08, open).

## Sync gating

- **Sync flag off ⇒ no DB communication.** A user who turned sync off expects zero DB traffic; a maintenance write behind that expectation (backfill, migration) needs explicit call-out and sign-off in the PR ("with alpha only users, we can push this change through" — a one-time pass, not a precedent). Internal outcomes ("backfilled N nodes") report to PostHog only — never a user toast; "backfilled" is not user vocabulary.
  Check: every new DB write path names the user-visible flag/action that authorizes it; no toasts for internal bookkeeping.
  Learned: PR #1332 (mdroidian, 2026-08).

## Datalog (Roam queries)

- **Bind page vs block facts explicitly.** A query separating page-level and block-level values (e.g. edit times) must bind both `?page` and `?node` (`[?node :block/page ?page]`) — binding only `?node` silently collapses the two.
  Learned: PR #1147.

## Telemetry & errors

- **Caught errors report to PostHog, not `console.error`.** Any failure affecting a user action also gets a user-facing message (toast/alert). `console.error` is invisible to both users and us.
  Learned: PR #1214, ENG-1092.

## Schema files & migrations

- **`DROP` statements belong in migrations, not schema files.** Schemas describe the target state; migrations move between states, ideally idempotent and incremental (only re-process what changed).
  Learned: PR #315, #748.

You are an expert senior software engineer specializing in modern web development, with deep expertise in TypeScript, React, Next.js (App Router), and Tailwind CSS. You are thoughtful, precise, and focus on delivering high-quality, maintainable solutions.

This repository uses Turborepo.

## Apps & Packages

`apps`

- apps/website: The public-facing website for Discourse Graphs, Uses Next.js.
- apps/roam: The Roam Research extension that implements the Discourse Graph protocol.
- apps/obsidian: The Obsidian plugin that implements the Discourse Graph protocol.

`packages`

- packages/tailwind-config: Shared tailwind config

- packages/eslint-config: ESLint preset
- packages/ui: Core React components

## Git & Publishing Conventions

### Branch Naming

When working on Linear issues, prefer using the Linear-provided branch name when available. Linear automatically generates branch names in the format `eng-####-descriptive-name` (e.g., `eng-1912-scaffold-repocontent-model`).

- Use Linear's generated branch name for consistency and traceability
- Branch names should be lowercase with hyphens separating words
- Include the Linear ticket ID at the start of the branch name

### Pull Request Titles

PR titles for Linear-backed work should follow this format:

- Format: `ENG-#### Ticket title`
- The ticket ID must be uppercased (e.g., `ENG-1912` not `eng-1912`)
- Follow the ticket ID with the exact Linear ticket title
- Example: `ENG-1912 Scaffold @repo/content-model`

### Pull Request Bodies

When creating or updating a pull request body:

- Start with `.github/pull_request_template.md`. Preserve its headings and guidance instead of adding substitute sections.
- Treat the Linear ticket as the source of truth. Do not restate it in the pull request body.
- Do not add a file-by-file summary, implementation diary, investigation log, full command output, or unrelated pre-existing issues.
- Put line-specific implementation context in inline GitHub comments.
- Put any non-obvious rules that future changes must preserve in code comments, tests, or documentation, not only in the pull request.
- Remove empty optional sections and anything that does not help review the diff.

## Style Guide

### UI Guidelines

- Use Tailwind CSS for styling where possible
- When refactoring inline styles, use tailwind classes
- Use platform-native UI components (see below) first with shadcn/ui as a fallback
- Maintain visual consistency with the host application's design system
- Follow responsive design principles

### TypeScript Guidelines

- Prefer `type` over `interface`
- Use explicit return types for functions
- Avoid `any` types when possible
- Prefer arrow functions over regular function declarations
- Use named parameters (object destructuring) when a function has more than 2 parameters

### Code Formatting

- Use Prettier with the project's configuration
- Maintain consistent naming conventions:
  - PascalCase for components and types
  - camelCase for variables and functions
  - UPPERCASE for constants

### Code Organization

- Prefer small, focused functions over inline code
- Extract complex logic into well-named functions
- Function names should describe their purpose clearly
- Choose descriptive function names that make comments unnecessary
- Break down complex operations into smaller, meaningful functions
- Prefer early returns over nested conditionals for better readability
- Prefer util functions for reusable logic and common operations

### Documentation

- Add comments only when necessary; descriptive names should minimize the need for comments
- Explain the why, not the what, focusing on reasoning, trade-offs, and approaches
- Document limitations, known bugs, or edge cases where behavior may not align with expectations
- Prefer sentence case in documentation and feature descriptions; capitalize official product/plugin names and exact UI labels, buttons, or titles, but keep generic feature terms lowercase to emphasize user actions

### Testing

- Write unit tests for new functionality
- Ensure tests are meaningful and maintainable
- Expose workspace unit tests through a `test:unit` script so the root validation command includes them
- Before opening a pull request or declaring work PR-ready, run `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` followed by `pnpm ci:validate` from the repository root, and resolve any failures
- After opening or updating an authorized pull request, wait for its required GitHub checks and report their final status

# Figma MCP Integration Rules

These rules guide AI coding agents when implementing Figma designs for the Discourse Graphs project. This is a Turborepo monorepo with three apps (website, Roam extension, Obsidian plugin) and shared packages.

## Design Token System

### Colors

- **Primary**: `#FF8C4B` (coral/orange) — brand color
- **Secondary**: `#5F57C0` (purple) — accent color
- **Neutral Dark**: `#1F1F1F`
- **Neutral Light**: `#F1F1F1`
- Shared Tailwind config: `packages/tailwind-config/tailwind.config.ts`
- CSS variables (shadcn/ui style) defined in `packages/ui/src/globals.css`:
  - `--primary`, `--secondary`, `--accent`, `--destructive`, `--muted`, `--background`, `--foreground`, `--border`, `--card`
  - HSL-based values with light/dark mode support via `.dark` class
- IMPORTANT: Never hardcode hex colors in shared components — use Tailwind theme tokens or CSS variables

### Typography

- System font stack (no custom fonts)
- Standard Tailwind text sizes: `text-sm`, `text-base`, `text-lg`, etc.
- Common weights: `font-medium`, `font-semibold`, `font-bold`

### Spacing & Layout

- Standard Tailwind spacing scale
- Common patterns: `gap-2`, `gap-4`, `p-1`, `p-2`, `p-6`, `px-3`, `py-2`
- Default border radius: `0.5rem` (`--radius`)

## Component Organization

### Shared UI Components (`packages/ui/`)

- Location: `packages/ui/src/components/ui/`
- Built on: Radix UI primitives + CVA (class-variance-authority) + Tailwind
- Available: Button, Card, Label, Checkbox, Select, Textarea, Badge
- Utility: `cn()` from `packages/ui/src/lib/utils.ts` (clsx + tailwind-merge)
- IMPORTANT: Always check `packages/ui/` for existing components before creating new ones

Import pattern:
```typescript
import { Button } from "@repo/ui/components/button"
import { cn } from "@repo/ui/lib/utils"
```

### Component Architecture Pattern

All shared components follow the shadcn/ui pattern:
```typescript
type ButtonProps = React.ButtonHTMLAttributes<HTMLButtonElement> &
  VariantProps<typeof buttonVariants> & { asChild?: boolean }

const Button = React.forwardRef<HTMLButtonElement, ButtonProps>(
  ({ className, variant, size, asChild = false, ...props }, ref) => {
    const Comp = asChild ? Slot : "button"
    return <Comp className={cn(buttonVariants({ variant, size, className }))} ref={ref} {...props} />
  }
)
```

### Naming Conventions

- PascalCase: Components and types (`Button`, `CardHeader`, `DiscourseNode`)
- camelCase: Variables, functions, props (`buttonVariants`, `cn`, `asyncSearch`)
- UPPERCASE: Constants (`WHITE_LOGO_SVG`, `MAX_ITEMS_PER_TYPE`)

## Platform-Specific Rules

### Website (`apps/website/`)

- **Framework**: Next.js 15 (App Router)
- **Components**: Uses `@repo/ui` shared components
- **Styling**: Shared Tailwind config + `@tailwindcss/typography`
- **Icons**: `lucide-react`
- **Path alias**: `~/app/*`
- Components in `apps/website/app/components/`

### Roam Extension (`apps/roam/`)

- **UI Framework**: BlueprintJS v3.50.4 — IMPORTANT: use Blueprint components (Menu, MenuItem, Popover, Button, Dialog, Tabs, Intent) for Roam-native look
- **Does NOT use** `@repo/ui` — stays native to Roam's design system
- **Styling**: Tailwind used sparingly for layout; CSS modules for component styles
- **Path alias**: `~/src/*`
- **Icon system**: Blueprint icons
- Components in `apps/roam/src/components/`
- Styles in `apps/roam/src/styles/`

### Obsidian Plugin (`apps/obsidian/`)

- **UI**: Custom React components targeting Obsidian's native look
- **Styling**: Tailwind mapped to Obsidian CSS variables:
  ```
  colors: {
    primary: "var(--background-primary)",
    secondary: "var(--background-secondary)",
    normal: "var(--text-normal)",
    accent: { DEFAULT: "var(--interactive-accent)" }
  }
  ```
- **Path alias**: `~/src/*`
- Components in `apps/obsidian/src/components/`

## Figma Implementation Workflow

### Required flow (do not skip)

1. Run `get_design_context` first to fetch the structured representation for the exact node(s)
2. If the response is too large or truncated, run `get_metadata` to get the high-level node map, then re-fetch only the required node(s)
3. Run `get_screenshot` for a visual reference
4. Identify which app/platform the design targets (website, Roam, or Obsidian)
5. Translate using the correct platform conventions:
   - **Website**: Use `@repo/ui` components + Tailwind + lucide-react icons
   - **Roam**: Use BlueprintJS components + Blueprint icons + CSS modules
   - **Obsidian**: Use custom React + Tailwind mapped to Obsidian CSS variables
6. Validate against Figma screenshot for 1:1 visual parity

### Implementation rules

- Treat Figma MCP output (React + Tailwind) as a design reference, not final code
- Reuse existing components from `packages/ui/` or the target app's component directory
- Use the project's color system and spacing tokens consistently
- Respect existing routing, state management, and data-fetch patterns
- Prefer `type` over `interface` for TypeScript types
- Use explicit return types for functions
- Use arrow functions over regular function declarations
- Use named parameters (object destructuring) when a function has more than 2 parameters

## Asset Handling

- IMPORTANT: If the Figma MCP server returns a localhost source for an image or SVG, use that source directly
- IMPORTANT: DO NOT import/add new icon packages — all assets should come from the Figma payload
- IMPORTANT: DO NOT create placeholders if a localhost source is provided
- SVG icons are stored as inline string constants in `icons.ts` files
- Static assets for website: `apps/website/public/`
- Website uses Lucide React for icons; Roam uses Blueprint icons; Obsidian uses inline SVGs

## Cross-Package Imports

```typescript
// Shared packages
import { Button } from "@repo/ui/components/button"
import sharedConfig from "@repo/tailwind-config"
import { DGSupabaseClient } from "@repo/database/lib/client"
import type { DiscourseNode } from "@repo/types"
```

Package exports are defined in each package's `package.json` exports field. Always use the package alias (`@repo/*`), not relative paths across packages.

- [feedback_obsidian_no_console.md](feedback_obsidian_no_console.md) - No console.warn/log/error in apps/obsidian — use new Notice() for user-facing errors

- [feedback_checkpoint_non_ticket_folder.md](feedback_checkpoint_non_ticket_folder.md) - Use a descriptive folder name (not branch name) for non-ticket checkpoint sessions

=== create-pr SKILL.md ===
     1	---
     2	name: create-pr
     3	description: >-
     4	  Open a pull request after a self-review pass: trim comments to one-liners,
     5	  check the diff against AGENTS.md, and write a reviewer-oriented PR body.
     6	user_invocable: true
     7	---
     8	
     9	# Create PR
    10	
    11	Get the branch reviewer-ready, then open the PR. Work the three phases in order —
    12	the self-review changes the diff, and the diff is what the body describes.
    13	
    14	## Phase 0 — Run `/pre-pr-review` first
    15	
    16	Invoke the `pre-pr-review` skill on this change set before anything below, and resolve
    17	its findings (fix, or state the deferral + ticket in the PR body). It is the deeper
    18	verification pass — mechanical greps against the diff, the data-layer invariants, and the
    19	frontend rules — and its outputs feed Phase 3: the draft annotations become line comments
    20	on the PR, the parity table and deferrals become body bullets. Skip it only if the user
    21	says they already ran it this session.
    22	
    23	`ARGUMENTS` may name a base branch. Otherwise infer it: if this branch was built on
    24	another open PR's branch, target that branch and say so in the body; else `main`.
    25	
    26	## Phase 1 — Trim the comments
    27	
    28	Only comments **you added on this branch**. Never rewrite comments that belong to
    29	committed work — it inflates the diff with churn a reviewer has to read past.
    30	
    31	```bash
    32	git diff --stat "$BASE"...HEAD
    33	git diff "$BASE"...HEAD | grep -nE '^\+\s*(//|/\*|\*|\{/\*)'
    34	```
    35	
    36	**Every surviving comment is one line.** Multi-line blocks and JSDoc paragraphs get
    37	compressed, not preserved.
    38	
    39	**Keep** a comment only when it says something the code cannot:
    40	
    41	- A platform or build quirk with a non-obvious cause — a host CSS rule that outranks
    42	  a utility class, a missing preflight, a library default that bites.
    43	- A deliberate choice a reader would otherwise "fix": an uncontrolled input, a
    44	  suppressed default, a two-step interaction, a guard that looks redundant.
    45	- Why an obvious simpler approach does *not* work.
    46	- A layout or structural decision that is easy to tidy up and thereby break.
    47	- A cross-file invariant that is invisible from this file alone.
    48	
    49	**Delete** a comment when it:
    50	
    51	- Restates the line below it, or narrates what a well-named function already says.
    52	- Defends a choice nobody would reverse (the ordinary, expected implementation).
    53	- Documents code that no longer exists after a rewrite.
    54	- Is a section banner or a decorative divider.
    55	
    56	Ambiguity test: *if I deleted this, would a competent reviewer make a wrong change?*
    57	No → delete it.
    58	
    59	## Phase 2 — Self-review the diff
    60	
    61	Read the repo's own rules first and check the diff against them, because these are
    62	exactly the comments a reviewer or bot will leave:
    63	
    64	```bash
    65	cat AGENTS.md CLAUDE.md STYLE_GUIDE.md 2>/dev/null
    66	find . -name AGENTS.md -not -path '*/node_modules/*'   # per-app rules override the root
    67	```
    68	
    69	Fix anything the diff violates. Common catches:
    70	
    71	- Inline `style={{...}}` for a static value where a utility class works. Computed
    72	  values (per-item colours) legitimately stay inline.
    73	- Hand-rolled CSS where the platform exposes a variable or an existing class.
    74	- `type` vs `interface`; missing explicit return types; `any`.
    75	- Function declarations where the codebase uses arrow functions.
    76	- Positional-index assumptions across two lists that can differ.
    77	- Console logging in apps that require a user-facing notice instead.
    78	- New dependencies where the platform already ships an equivalent.
    79	
    80	Then the checks the CI will run, and the project's own verification story:
    81	
    82	```bash
    83	pnpm check-types && pnpm lint      # in the changed app
    84	npx prettier --check <changed files>
    85	```
    86	
    87	If the change is observable at runtime, exercise it and say so in the body with
    88	concrete numbers. A body that claims "verified" without saying how is worth less
    89	than one that names what was measured.
    90	
    91	## Phase 3 — Write the body and open it
    92	
    93	Lead with what the reviewer needs to decide, not with a narration of the diff — they
    94	can read the diff. Keep it scannable; drop any section that would be empty.
    95	
    96	```markdown
    97	<One or two sentences: the problem, and the shape of the fix.>
    98	
    99	## Review focus
   100	
   101	- `path/to/file.ts` — <what to look at here and why it matters>
   102	- <the riskiest change, named explicitly>
   103	
   104	## Decisions worth challenging
   105	
   106	- **<Decision>** — <why this way, and the alternative rejected.>
   107	- <Any deviation from the ticket or from a sibling implementation, and why.>
   108	
   109	## Verification
   110	
   111	- <checks run>
   112	- <runtime evidence, with numbers>
   113	- <what is deliberately not covered, e.g. no unit tests and why>
   114	
   115	## Known limits
   116	
   117	<Edge cases documented rather than fixed, and why that is the right call. Omit if none.>
   118	```
   119	
   120	Rules for the body:
   121	
   122	- Name files by path so the reviewer can jump straight to them.
   123	- Surface deviations from the ticket yourself. A reviewer who finds one unmentioned
   124	  distrusts the rest.
   125	- State what you did *not* do and why — no tests, an edge case left alone, scope held.
   126	- If the diff is large, justify the coupling: what single problem it solves and why
   127	  the files must land together.
   128	
   129	Title: `ENG-#### Exact Linear ticket title` (ticket id uppercased).
   130	
   131	```bash
   132	gh pr create --base "$BASE" --title "..." --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
   133	...
   134	EOF
   135	)"
   136	```
   137	
   138	End the body with:
   139	
   140	```
   141	🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
   142	```
   143	
   144	## After opening
   145	
   146	Report the URL, the base branch and why, and the diff size. If the branch is stacked,
   147	say which PR must merge first. Do not merge; do not mark ready-for-review beyond
   148	opening it.

=== dg-engineering-writing-style/SKILL.md ===
---
name: dg-engineering-writing-style
description: Draft and revise engineering emails, chat messages, requests, follow-ups, status updates, engineering tickets, PR comments, issue reports, release notes, technical documentation, and other team writing in the shared Discourse Graphs style. Use whenever a Discourse Graphs engineer asks to write, rewrite, phrase, shorten, clarify, or polish team communication or documentation, unless they request a different style.
---

# DG Engineering Writing Style

Write in a direct, concise, plainspoken style that preserves important context and qualification.

## Core style

- Lead with the relevant point and move quickly to the concrete question, request, or action.
- Prefer the shortest version that remains clear and preserves necessary nuance.
